name: UC Santa Cruz

sources.label: UC Santa Cruz General Catalog (course descriptions)

notes: These are UC Santa Cruz courses that appear under 'Elective Courses' on the audit but likely fit a UC San Diego requirement once advising reviews them.
'likely' means the course matches the requirement's own rule, so advising should only need to apply it.
'petition' means it's a reasonable petition based on the course description, not a guarantee.
Codes are as they appear on the TSS audit. Some UCSC subjects were renamed (LALS shows as LAST, ART as ARTF).

courses.title: Rhetoric and Inquiry
courses.why: UCSC's second composition course. The audit's composition rule looks for 'composition' in course titles, so advising may need to apply this one by hand.

courses.title: Beginning Programming in Python
courses.why: An introductory programming course, which is what Information Technology Fluency asks for.

courses.title: Introduction to Latin American and Latino Studies
courses.why: An interdisciplinary social-science and history survey; could support Social Analysis or Narrative, Aesthetic and Historical Reasoning.

courses.title: AIDS Across the Americas
courses.why: A cultural and historical study course, closest to Narrative, Aesthetic and Historical Reasoning.

courses.title: Art and Social Change in Latin America
courses.why: An art-history and cultural-analysis course, closest to Narrative, Aesthetic and Historical Reasoning.

courses.title: Digital Tools for Contemporary Art Practice
courses.why: A studio art course where students make work, which is what Art Making asks for.

courses.title: Engineering Principles of Electronics
courses.why: Physics-based electronics with lab content; a possible petition for Analytic Methodologies/Scientific Method.
